execution_evidence.scope: Static repository source and all migration references; no live production or temporary PostgreSQL was accessed.

findings.title: Native storage onboarding omits the early authorization writer protocol
findings.trigger: action=activate in a fresh Native session transaction

evidence.claim: Public Native entry resolves storage_owner_v1 at declaration.
Locks the onboard attempt FOR UPDATE before activation.
Takes per-owner onboard lock, then owner/root advisory lock.
Calls private activation after those locks.
Private activation creates the Project through project_mutation_core_v2.
Adds authorization_writer_require_v2 at every project core BEGIN.

findings.outcome: The Native activation path has no authorization_writer_guard_v2/fanout entrance. Core entry should raise authorization_early_writer_guard_required and roll back activation; this is a product regression, not merely fixture ordering.

earliest_safe_patch.anchor: First body BEGIN, immediately before the input-validation IF and before issuer:=clued_private.issuer_resolve_identity_compatible_v1(...).
earliest_safe_patch.source_anchor: begin\n  if coalesce(length(p_issuer_secret),0)<32 or jsonb_typeof(p_input) is distinct from 'object'
earliest_safe_patch.recommended_protocol: For op='activate', take authorization_writer_guard_v2(u), recheck storage_owner_v1(), then authorization_writer_lock_fanout_v2(u). Keep all original issuer, Native session, attempt, run-token, expiry and downstream final validation.
earliest_safe_patch.rationale: Issuer resolution takes issuer credential/app FOR SHARE; expiry sweep and attempt take row locks. Taking the owner mutex in private activation or core is too late and would introduce inverted waits.

original_lock_order: storage_owner_v1: verified Native account and live auth.sessions FOR SHARE
issuer resolver: issuer credential/app FOR SHARE
storage_onboard_expire_v1: expired attempts FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
private activation -> project core currentness lock and receipt -> Project INSERT/future fanout

session_wait_checks.claim: storage_owner_v1 verifies authorization_owner_v12, session_id, matching auth.sessions owner and wall-clock not_after, with FOR SHARE.
After activation and lock waits, the public entry re-runs storage_owner_v1 and checks attempt expires_at using clock_timestamp; failure rolls back all activation effects.
Issuer resolver verifies active credential, wall-clock valid_until and live issuer/app after FOR SHARE waits.

required_verification: A real Native public activation in a fresh transaction succeeds without any test-only early-writer trigger.
Its newly created owned Project gets exact contexts:* contributions; an owned Context created under it gets the same environment-specific macro authority.
Native activation waits at the owner authorization mutex before holding onboard/app/Project/Binding locks.
Race activation versus macro approval/reduction/revocation in both orders; resulting authorization is current and complete, and deleted/denied authority is not resurrected.
Native session expiry and attempt expiry while waiting refuse and leave no Project/authorization/grant/connection partial effects.
Private project core still refuses without early guard; no late guard is added to bypass this invariant.
findings.coverage_gap: all-contexts-authorization-locks-db.test.mjs exercises gateway Project creation and Native Context creation, but contains no storage onboarding case. Existing resource-center-storage-onboard-db.fixture.mjs uses real Native public activation; its harness defers gateway closeout and may fail earlier at new serialization qualification, so its existence is not evidence that the new activation path works.

findings.title: Unnecessary patch changes a frozen, retired legacy alias
findings.recommendation: Remove only this alias from the project_entrances patch list. Preserve project_mutation_core require and Native clued_user_project_mutate guard/fanout, and retain all current gateway v2 writer protocol.

evidence.claim: Actual Worker tool routes clued_project_mutate to clued_project_mutate_v2.
Only retained business caller is clued_oauth_call, which invokes the retired resolver before its alias branch.
Legacy alias is separately frozen outside current Worker80/CI8.
Alias loses PUBLIC/anon execution and receives no gateway grant; non-anonymous existing ACL preserved.
Original alias explicitly revoked authenticated execution.

findings.qualification: Static call graph supports the recommendation. Actual final catalog OID/source/ACL and negative calls still require runtime tests. Preserve frozen CLOSEOUT SQL and do not rewrite its historical hash to accommodate this unnecessary patch.
required_verification: Legacy alias prosrc SHA, OID, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and ACL unchanged across new successors.
Anon and gateway direct calls denied; authenticated direct call remains denied under the actual final catalog. Inspect service_role/existing non-anonymous entries rather than assuming their absence.
Legacy OAuth rejects before the alias branch and creates no receipt or Project.
Direct private old/new project cores without early guard still fail closed.
Supported Native old/new project mutations and gateway v2 mutation really succeed and preserve early mutex/fanout behavior.
Replaying frozen closeout after the successors remains valid without weakening its manifest/source drift checks.

inventory_boundary: All SQL references to the four private project cores across migrations were searched. Project INSERTs are present in observe_core, old mutation_core and v2 mutation_core only. P5 gateway performs updates, not Project creation, and has no direct call to these cores. No dynamic string call beyond migration patch signature lists was found.
decision_limits: This report is independent static review evidence, not an Owner approval, passing runtime test, production acceptance or completion of the original eight-view Task.
